name: Stubai Glacier

source.note: Piste reference data — confirm at source. Approximate Mutterberg valley station at the head of the Stubai valley; the nearest village, Neustift im Stubaital, is about 20 km down-valley
Official Stubai Glacier news: 'Located at an altitude of 1,749m to 3,212m'; 'At 3,212 metres, the mountain station of the Wildspitz lift is the highest point'. Vertical derived.

Search summary: 36 runs and 65 km (fall line): 17 blue (23 km), 11 red (14 km), 1 black (2 km) and 7 ski routes (18 km). Those parts add up to 57 km, so no percentage split is derived. 26 lifts: 5 gondolas (including the 3S Eisgratbahn), 7 chairlifts, 10 T-bars and 4 practice lifts/magic carpets (other). Total capacity 43,781 persons/hour per skiresort.info (https://www.skiresort.info/ski-resort/stubai-glacier-stubaier-gletscher/test-result/lifts-cable-cars/); another result gives 44,084.
Piste reference data — confirm at source. Only features Piste is confident about are set; everything else is unknown (null), not 'not offered'. Ski schools and rental shops operate at the bases

character: The largest glacier ski area in Austria (per results), at the head of the Stubai valley about 40 km from Innsbruck, with skiing between 1,750 m and 3,210 m from October into May. The 3S Eisgratbahn brings skiers up from the Mutterberg valley station, with the Gamsgarten gondola as an alternative.
learning: Reference note: the glacier has blue runs and a ski school at the Gamsgarten level, but high-altitude conditions can be cold and windy. Confirm beginner areas and lessons.
